reviews.title: Testing Solubility of Common Substances
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Compare how common solid substances dissolve in water and distinguish soluble from insoluble materials.

procedure_summary.instruction: Label one transparent cup for each test substance and add the same volume of water.
procedure_summary.observation: Each cup starts with a clear, equal-volume water sample.

procedure_summary.instruction: Add an equal small amount of salt, sugar, or sand to its labeled cup.
procedure_summary.observation: The solid is visible in each cup before stirring.

procedure_summary.instruction: Stir each cup for the same amount of time.
procedure_summary.observation: Salt and sugar disappear into the water, while sand remains visible and settles.

procedure_summary.instruction: Classify each substance as soluble or insoluble in water.
procedure_summary.observation: The results can be compared in a simple observation table.

reviews.title: Separating a Sand and Salt Mixture
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Demonstrate filtration, evaporation, and recovery of components from a sand and salt mixture.

procedure_summary.instruction: Add water to the sand and salt mixture and stir thoroughly.
procedure_summary.observation: Salt dissolves while sand remains as solid particles.

procedure_summary.instruction: Pour the mixture through folded filter paper in a funnel.
procedure_summary.observation: Sand remains on the filter paper and salt solution collects below.

procedure_summary.instruction: Transfer the filtrate to an evaporating dish and warm it gently.
procedure_summary.observation: Water evaporates and solid salt crystals remain.

procedure_summary.instruction: Compare the recovered sand and salt with the original mixture.
procedure_summary.observation: Both components are recovered by using different physical properties.

reviews.title: Diffusion of an Ink Drop in Water
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Observe diffusion and relate the spreading of particles to temperature and particle motion.

procedure_summary.instruction: Fill one beaker with cold water and one with warm water.
procedure_summary.observation: The two beakers contain equal-looking water at different temperatures.

procedure_summary.instruction: Place one drop of ink gently in the center of each beaker without stirring.
procedure_summary.observation: A dark ink region appears at the point of addition.

procedure_summary.instruction: Observe both beakers for the same time interval.
procedure_summary.observation: Ink spreads through warm water faster than through cold water.

procedure_summary.instruction: Record the relative diffusion rates and explain the observation using particle motion.
procedure_summary.observation: Higher temperature is associated with faster visible spreading.

reviews.title: Law of Conservation of Mass
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Compare total mass before and after a chemical reaction in a closed system.

procedure_summary.instruction: Place baking soda in a balloon and vinegar in a flask without mixing them.
procedure_summary.observation: Reactants are separated while the complete apparatus can be weighed.

procedure_summary.instruction: Attach the balloon to the flask and measure the mass of the closed arrangement.
procedure_summary.observation: The initial total mass is recorded.

procedure_summary.instruction: Lift the balloon so the baking soda falls into the vinegar.
procedure_summary.observation: Fizzing occurs and the balloon inflates as gas forms.

procedure_summary.instruction: Measure the mass again without opening the arrangement.
procedure_summary.observation: The total mass remains approximately unchanged in the closed system.

reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Classify household solutions as acidic, basic, or neutral using safe indicator color changes.

procedure_summary.observation: The samples are arranged for side-by-side comparison.

procedure_summary.instruction: Touch blue and red litmus paper to each sample using clean droppers.
procedure_summary.observation: Acidic and basic samples produce opposite litmus changes.

procedure_summary.instruction: Add universal indicator to fresh portions of the samples.
procedure_summary.observation: Different colors indicate different approximate pH values.

reviews.title: Reaction of Iron Nails with Copper Sulphate
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Observe a displacement reaction and connect visible changes to relative reactivity of metals.

procedure_summary.instruction: Clean an iron nail with sandpaper and place it in a test tube of blue copper sulphate solution.
procedure_summary.observation: The nail is initially metallic gray and the solution is blue.

procedure_summary.instruction: Leave the nail immersed without shaking for an observation period.
procedure_summary.observation: A reddish-brown coating begins forming on the nail.

procedure_summary.instruction: Remove the nail and compare the solution color with a fresh sample.
procedure_summary.observation: The solution becomes less blue as iron displaces copper.

procedure_summary.instruction: Write the word equation for the displacement reaction.
procedure_summary.observation: Iron and copper sulphate produce iron sulphate and copper.

reviews.title: Preparation of a Standard Solution
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Practice accurate weighing, dissolution, transfer, and dilution while preparing a solution of known concentration.

procedure_summary.instruction: Calculate and weigh the required mass of a suitable soluble reagent.
procedure_summary.observation: The balance reading is recorded to the required precision.

procedure_summary.instruction: Dissolve the reagent in a small volume of distilled water in a beaker.
procedure_summary.observation: The solid dissolves to form a clear or uniformly colored solution.

procedure_summary.instruction: Transfer the solution quantitatively into a volumetric flask and rinse the beaker.
procedure_summary.observation: Rinse portions are added so the dissolved material is transferred completely.

procedure_summary.instruction: Make the volume up to the calibration mark and mix by inversion.
procedure_summary.observation: A homogeneous standard solution with known concentration is obtained.

reviews.title: Effect of Concentration on an Equilibrium
reviews.subject: Chemistry
reviews.summary: Observe a reversible color change and relate it qualitatively to a change in reactant concentration.

procedure_summary.instruction: Place equal portions of the equilibrium mixture into labeled test tubes.
procedure_summary.observation: Each tube begins with a comparable color.

procedure_summary.instruction: Add a measured amount of reagent to one tube and water to another comparison tube.
procedure_summary.observation: The tubes now have different concentrations of the reacting species.

procedure_summary.instruction: Mix gently and compare the colors under the same lighting.
procedure_summary.observation: The equilibrium mixture shifts color after the concentration change.

procedure_summary.instruction: Record the direction of the visible shift and identify the applied change.
procedure_summary.observation: The color change provides qualitative evidence of equilibrium adjustment.
